english.title: Onwardly disclose personal information disclosed by Welsh Revenue Authority under s.64(1) for research purposes
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having received personal information **(..GIVE DETAILS OF INFORMATION..) that was disclosed by the Welsh Revenue Authority under section 64(1) of the Digital Economy Act 2017 for research purposes, further disclosed that information
english.legislation: Contrary to section 68(2), (8) and (10) of the Digital Economy Act 2017.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
It is a defence for a person charged with an offence under subsection (8) to prove that the person reasonably believed -
(a) that the disclosure was lawful, or
(b) that the information had already and lawfully been made available to the public (section 68(9) of the Digital Economy Act 2017).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 68(11) of the Digital Economy Act 2017 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
